data.name: Ui.Settings.Intro
data.value: SpicetifyDeck drives the Spotify desktop client through a Spicetify extension. This page shows every link in that chain, so a failure can be pinned to the one that is broken.

data.name: Ui.Settings.RequiresApply
data.value: The bridge file was updated because the Macro Deck address changed, but Spicetify has not applied it yet. Run Repair Bridge, then restart Spotify.

data.name: Issues.NoSpicetify.Description
data.value: SpicetifyDeck drives the Spotify client through a Spicetify extension, so nothing works until Spicetify is installed. The Spicetify command line tool was not found on this computer.

data.name: Issues.NoSpicetify.Resolve
data.value: Install Spicetify from spicetify.app, run spicetify apply, then run the Install Spicetify Bridge action.

data.name: Issues.NoBridge.Title
data.value: The bridge is not installed yet

data.name: Issues.NoBridge.Description
data.value: Spicetify is installed, so this is one step away from working. The SpicetifyDeck bridge is a separate file that belongs in Spicetify's Extensions folder and has not been written yet. Run the Install Spicetify Bridge action once, then restart Spotify. Nothing else is needed: the action writes the file, configures Spicetify and applies the change for you, so there is no command to run by hand.

data.name: Issues.NoBridge.Resolve
data.value: Run the Install Spicetify Bridge action, then restart Spotify.

data.name: Issues.NotConnected.Description
data.value: The bridge is installed and Spicetify is configured to load it, but the Spotify client has stopped reporting through it. That normally means the client was closed, or it failed and is showing its own error screen. Start Spotify again; if it goes straight back to an error screen, run Repair Spicetify Bridge with Spotify completely closed. Never run a bridge action while Spotify is open, because applying a change rewrites the client and can break a running Spotify.

data.name: Issues.NotConnected.Resolve
data.value: Quit Spotify completely and start it again. If it is still not connected, run Repair Spicetify Bridge with Spotify closed.

data.name: Issues.Corrupted.Description
data.value: A bridge file is present but unusable, usually because it still holds an unsubstituted placeholder or a token from an earlier run of SpicetifyDeck. Repair rewrites it and re-applies Spicetify, keeping the current token.

data.name: Issues.Corrupted.Resolve
data.value: Run the Repair Spicetify Bridge action, then restart Spotify.

data.name: Issues.AuthFailed.Description
data.value: The Spotify client connected but presented an authentication token this plugin did not issue, so it was refused and no state was read. Repair rewrites the bridge file with the current token.

data.name: Issues.AuthFailed.Resolve
data.value: Run the Repair Spicetify Bridge action, then restart Spotify.

data.name: Issues.UpdatePending.Title
data.value: Bridge update waiting for a restart

data.name: Issues.UpdatePending.Description
data.value: The bridge on disk is newer than the one Spotify is running. Spotify loads an extension only when it starts, so it is still using the previous copy and that copy keeps working. Quit Spotify completely and start it again to pick up the new bridge. Do not reset the authentication: the bridge Spotify is running and this plugin already share the same token.

data.name: Issues.UpdatePending.Resolve
data.value: Quit Spotify completely and start it again, or run Repair Spicetify Bridge while Spotify is closed.

data.name: Issues.Unknown.Resolve
data.value: That issue is not one this plugin knows about.

data.name: Actions.Bridge.Install.Description
data.value: Find Spicetify, write the bridge into its Extensions folder, configure it to load, apply the change, and verify all of it. The existing authentication token is kept, so an install can never leave Spotify and this plugin holding different tokens. From 2.1.0 the address is a fixed port, so this only has to be done once. Spotify must be quit and started again afterwards, because Spicetify loads extensions into the client only when it applies and when the client starts.

data.name: Actions.Bridge.ResetAuth.Description
data.value: Generate a new authentication token and rewrite the bridge to match. The bridge Spotify is running is refused until you quit Spotify and run this again, which is the point. Use it only when the token is genuinely lost or a bridge is holding one this plugin no longer accepts. Nothing else rotates the token.

data.name: Actions.Bridge.Errors.Failed
data.value: The bridge operation did not finish. See the plugin log for details.

data.name: Actions.Bridge.Reinstall.Description
data.value: Write, configure, apply and verify the bridge again, keeping the current authentication token. Use this after updating SpicetifyDeck, or if the installed bridge is pointing at an address from an older version. Quit Spotify before running it, then start Spotify again.

data.name: Actions.Bridge.Repair.Description
data.value: Rewrite the bridge file and re-apply Spicetify, keeping the current authentication token. Use this when the bridge is installed but not connecting, or when Spotify is still holding an address from an earlier version. Quit Spotify first, then start it again.

data.name: Actions.Bridge.Restart.Description
data.value: Drop the current bridge connection so the Spotify client reconnects on its own. Useful when the bridge is installed and configured but has stopped reporting.

data.name: Actions.Bridge.Uninstall.Description
data.value: Remove SpicetifyDeck from the Spicetify configuration and delete the bridge file. Every other extension you have is left exactly as it was.

data.name: Variables.DeckConnectionStatus.Description
data.value: Where the bridge has got to: Spicetify Not Installed, Bridge Not Installed, Bridge Corrupted, Bridge Installed - Waiting for Spotify, Bridge Disconnected, Authentication Failed, Bridge Update Pending, or Bridge Connected.

data.name: Variables.DeckSpotifyConnected.Description
data.value: Whether a Spotify client is connected to the bridge and reporting its state.
